author: Frosty
text:
HW - Flag Limits 14 This attempt at in-depth analysis of FLs was done in just above 2 hours. I know some of you can draw this up in seconds By far, this is the hardest RTM material, personally, for me to grasp.

When I was finishing the HW, I tried my best not to look at the right side and try to mark things off after moving bar-by-bar. I do this to avoid positive outcome bias (if this is the right term for it), i.e. not looking for the results first and then finding the reason why. What I did was the reverse, i.e. mark the zones first and then look at the reactions later.

When drawing up FLs, I remember what bro Staurum said: without FTR, there is no FL without break there is no FTR without a zone or price barrier, there is no break without price movement, there is no zone or price barrier What I understand the progression of thought is:price movement - barriers/zones - break of barriers - FTR - FL The logical step from that, then, would be:find important barriers, look for their breaks, draw FTRs, assess which are the FLs I will document the steps and thought process that I use in this HW. If it is not too much to ask, I would love to hear any opinions from all of you regarding my thought process when looking for FLs. I might be doing the wrong things and, therefore, over/undercomplicating this. A simple yes/no will suffice, if you all have the time and will to comment, that is Monthly Chart: Find the clearest important barrier starts from this TF for best / largest amounts of pips reaction. This one clearly has an important SR flip level at a BRN at 1.37000 (purple line). I then mark this off in the Monthly chart. I start analyzing at the region of the big bearish candle that breaks the important SR flip from above (shown on the chart)

Weekly Chart: I drew the red thick FL from the break of the important SR flip. This also coincides with the break of a local low (blue line). I trace the chart to the right and found a trick level below (blue box). That was all that I marked the first time.

Daily Chart: After the above two charts are done, I went down to the D1 TF. Here, I marked FTB, 2TB, and 3TB.

H4 Chart #1: In the H4 TF, I mark the FTR after the break of an important barrier in the LTF (two highs that lines up). Looking back on the D1 chart, I can clearly see now that the level is a FL since it held price up a couple of times before the LQ described on the previous D1 chart.

H4 Chart #2: I mark FTB and 2TB to the upper green FL. I can clearly see the LQ base (Pre-CP) and I marked this on the chart. I also marked the swap FL (purple box) from engulfing the top green FL.

I can see FTB and 2TB to the purple FL but I didn't mark these on the chart.

The LS kink (bottom green box) is then drawn after looking at the H1 chart, which also coincides with the engulfing of a CPPAZ on H1.

I then mark the engulf that hasn't reached its target (the pre-CP MPL).

Then lastly, the potential BSZ because of the 2 similar lows. This 2 lows touches the mouth of the LS kink and the previous moves haven't touched the LS kink level. I guessed that this would be used for future fakeout to the MPL of the LS kink.

H4 Chart #3: I marked the reaction further on the right side of the LS kink.

PA clearly shows the DM forming to touch the exact LS kink level (thin blue box).

Personally, the SL for any trade I will take should be placed beyond the trick zone (thin blue box)

The target for the long is the pre-CP MPL, which clearly is hit later on.

That was a long explanation, lol. I hope I get some things right this time. I really tried to keep things in the simplest manner I could.

Thank you everyone for your continued guidance and comments. I appreciate them as always

author: Frosty
text:
After doing so many homeworks, I think it is a good idea to open a demo account and start trying to piece all of the pieces together by analyzing the charts and placing demo trades.

All trades will be posted, win or lose, along with the reasoning behind them, complete with SL, TP and any trade managements done during the trade.

There are 6 pairs that I'll be using for this studying purpose: AUD/JPY, EUR/GBP, NZD/USD, USD/CAD, NOK/SEK, XAU/USD The only reason why I chose these pairs: they seem to have weak correlation with each other (....and because I love Canada and Scandinavia ) I personally dislike CHF for some reason, so I think I'll leave CHF pairs for the future Money management rule for risk is 1% of total account balance per trade or 0.5% if I feel less confident about a setup. I'll be treating this account as real money account. Still trying to find a way on how to adjust the % if there are many open trades but I'll get there in the future.

The main purpose, to be honest, is to get feedback on analysis of trades, whether it is correct or incorrect. The second major reason is to train my chicken mentality of not placing trades due to the fear of losses. If I did my analysis, I should have the confidence to trade it. Bro Staurum also mentioned this once in reply to one of my post:If we are always second guessing, we cannot trade.

If the trade is a win, great, I'll learn from those and that means some or all of my analysis is correct or mostly correct. If it is a loss, all the better, I will learn from those more than I learn from the winning trades, then use the lesson as a feedback for the next trades so I don't make the same mistakes. And most of all, I believe all of you here will guide me through my losing trades when you have the time. Account balance curve should be the last thing I should worry about because I understand that if I focus on the process of trading the right way, account balance curve will take care of itself.

After watching the "curing perfectionism" video on bro Staurum's journal, I now somehow understand the reason why I can't make progress is really mainly because of the fear of failure and I expect RTM method to work ALL THE TIME (100% accuracy) right from the very first time I place an order until the time to exit.

Mastery takes thousands of hours of practice, but I can't even start the first second of the journey just because I'm too afraid the trades will have many losses. I realized I was expecting a PERFECT, FLAWLESS method that can't lose 100% of the time, which I should understand by now that this expectation is just unrealistic. I also re-read Edge's markepedia article and that stands out in #1 (not surprising after understanding my own thought process)

If I find some trade setup that don't work, I keep scouring the charts endlessly for ways to optimize the trade and how to make them work out so no losses occur. Usually by widening the zones, changing the level i thought the entries should be in, curve fitting targets so the trades work out before reversing to SL level, etc.

My INTJ nature doesn't help in this case as well as I always beat myself up extra hard if something goes wrong or if I perceive something can go wrong (in my mind, those are losing trades). Bad self-talk happens or will happen inside my mind that says something along the lines of: "You're still not qualified to trade!", "You're still a noob, read everything again!", "You can never be a trader", "Your trade reasoning is crap!", etc.

So for me, the plan for the rest of this week is to finish up on reading and to understand each of the puzzle piece down to its sub-atomic particles as best as I can (while realizing that I can't truly understand it in one sitting and that understanding will improve through screen time and analysis time). Tomorrow, I'll open a perpetual demo account ready for next week, when I will start to analyze charts in real-time and place demo trades to start the training process.

Believe me, I'm not looking for any sympathy by typing up these words. The purpose is that I want to declare my fears out in the open so I can vanquish it and kill it down to its roots. Starting today, I will try my hardest to have faith in my abilities to improve. I will not blame outside circumstances for my current psychological condition, because if I blame external factors, I will never be able to control myself. I will focus on things that I can change first and that is myself.

I apologize for this rambling. I'll get back on track starting next post. Thank you all for taking the time to visit my journal Thank you all for your continued guidance.

author: Frosty
text:
Weekly Analysis and Training - Week 1 Hi all, I just opened a demo account on Friday. It is from FXPro, due to the ease of demo account management in their web control panel and its' non- expiring demo account property. I'll start with the training of RTM-style trading starting Monday. Hope to learn from all of you here I've done all past analysis from HTF to LTF for the 6 instruments that I mentioned a few days ago.

I've already noted where I'm going to look for PA on the LTF for each one of them.

I'm not going to trade blindly from any level. If a good trade level was found after my weekly analysis, I will skip them.

One of the many rules of my trading will be: DISCIPLINE. I will not chase trades. I will not force trades just for the sake of trading.

Below is one of my analysis on one of the pairs, Gold.

Monthly Chart In my humble opinion, price is trapped between these two boxes, i.e. the MPL of CPPAZ on the top, and the FL on the bottom.

Price already broke into the CPPAZ and currently retracing down to collect orders for additional fuel to reach the MPL.

I think from this scale, the previous information is the most we can get. Dropping to LTF next.

Weekly Chart From this scale, we can see that price is held down by the swap FL. The target, which is shown on the chart, is the FL from the engulf of a CPPAZ at the bottom, which also coincides with a LS (not marked) Price hasn't reached its target at the bottom FL and is currently retracing to collect more orders in the swap FL. At this point, we can't clearly see where the last set of clean orders are.

LTF needed for zooming in on potential trade areas.

The second weekly chart shows the structure of the price history on the left and what I think is worth noting, i.e. the FTR after the break of all-time high, the DP to break the all-time high, and the reactions off the FTR. BSZ has formed below D and the next time back not shown in the second chart.

Daily Chart We can now see where the last trick was played in the swap FL. This is the last clean sets of orders. Conveniently, there are many confluences that supports a trade inside the violet box, i.e. the trick area. Please see chart for what these confluences are.

M15 Chart A closer look at the trick area, with their FLs. On the chart is how I would enter the trade.

I will look for signs of approach PA to both of the marked areas, i.e. CP or CPLQ.

If one of those occurs, I'll TT the entry price levels. If there is no clear approach PA, I'll get in later using engulf-retrace on LTF If I miss it altogether, I will move on since trading and life doesn't end then and there Monthly Chart Revisited This is what I predict the ITs will do in the future (if one of that IT is me )

Hope is the bane of all traders and I don't hope this will happen. It is just a simple prediction based on my way of current thinking.

PA will definitely show the way and adjustments definitely will be made according to new information later on.

I will type up an elaborate trading plan for my personal use and to remind me of the rules that I should follow.

I'll post the plan here for all of you to guide and correct. I just realized that the markets give us freedom to do whatever we pleased.

We should create our own boundaries. From those boundaries, through persistence and feedback, we will create self-discipline. No boundaries, no self-discipline.

As always, please feel free to correct anything in my posts. Thank you all for your continued gems of wisdom

text:
@bro Linos: Thank you for the confirmation of the mantra, brother. If it works for you, I believe it will work for me too Next up is the creation of a trading plan. Obviously it will have a lot of flaws at first, but I believe it will improve with time.

After reanalyzing the speed of my chart analysis (which is in the snail pace category), I'll cut down on two more of the pairs that I will be watching, i.e. NZD/USD and NOK/SEK. NZD/USD is approximately inverse of USD/CAD, so this should be redundant. NOK/SEK looks blocky because exotics (for obvious reasons) have less trading volume.

So now I have only 4 focus pairs in my study list: AUD/JPY, EUR/GBP, USD/CAD, Gold.

That should cover most currencies and correlating trades shouldn't be a problem.

Trading volume is also sufficient to make the charts not looking square- ish/blocky.

As I said before, the choice is purely arbitrary other than correlation considerations.

Personal Trading Plan for Study Phase: - Objective of study phase:learn where is the most likely price level that price will bounce, annihilation of mentality - Starting capital (demo):$5,000 - Risk per trade:1% of total account balance per trade - Minimum RR ratio: 1:1.5 risk:reward (will improve with time and study) - Pairs to trade:AUD/JPY, EUR/GBP, USD/CAD, Gold - Entries:divided into two equal-risk parts at relevant zones, mainly to scale in - Reason for dividing entries:the objective is to find the larger FL that price will react to in study phase. Sniper accuracy will come later with screen time. - Stops:the same level for both entries.

- Reason for placing stops at the same price level:the SL level is the logical place on the chart where the trade is invalidated due to incorrect analysis. - Exits:exit the positions at first and second trouble areas, i.e. HTF SR.

FL, next origin of move, and keep the smallest lot possible to run indefinitely to see ultimately where price potentially goes to for learning process. *Side comment*: Not trying to divert attention from RTM materials, I remember I've read a good thread at FF regarding the benefit of keeping positions indefinitely. Here it is for anyone wants to read it. I will remove the link if it is inappropriate.

- Trade ALL setups that have been analyzed and personally judged as a good setup - Do not force trades that have not been analyzed. If a trade is missed, move on to the next opportunity. Don't chase trades - Do visualization exercises every morning and night. This is personalized, but basically it is a subconscious reprogramming technique that I learned from the book "Psychocybernetics" by Dr. Maxwell Maltz. I eliminated 100% of my road rage problem with this technique. I believe it will help me with trading and other endeavors too.

Tools and Color Schemes: Might as well standardize this too for ease of reanalyzing the trades.

MT4 Tools: - Rectangle Extender – Automatically extend boxes and lines.

- News Calendar – Shows upcoming and previous news (bottom right of chart).

- Drawing Tools – Used for drawing boxes and lines (bottom left of chart). - Spread and Lot Pip Indicator – Shows the spread, lot pip, and pair symbol (top right of chart).

Color Schemes: - Major High/Low – Red/Blue horizontal trend lines - Minor or Lower Timeframe High/Low – Violet/Green horizontal trend lines - Major Upper Flag Limit/Lower Flag Limit – Red/Blue hollow rectangles - Minor Upper Flag Limit/Lower Flag Limit – Violet/Green hollow rectangles - Clean orders, spiked orders, and MPL at Upper Flag Limit – Thistle, Violet, Khaki solid rectangles - Clean orders, spiked orders, and MPL at Lower Flag Limit – Powder Blue, Cornflower Blue, Pale Green solid rectangles

author: Frosty
text:
EUR/GBP Trade #1 - Trade Closed Closed all positions. The reason is because it looks like SL got close to being tagged, but the 1 pip SL buffer and adding the average spread actually saved me this time.

I closed the positions as soon as I see price already touched the kink of the red line (marked on the chart), which is the target for shorts after the engulf of CP area to the left. The high of the FL was at 0.91415 and price then went to 0.91424. My SL was at 0.91462. My general SL formula for shorts is: high of FL + 1 pip buffer + average spread for the pair rounded up (in this case it was 3.7 pips). Theoretically, my SL was hit and I should exit my positions. Theory and practice is really different After tagging the theoretical SL level, price turned and produced a nice bounce. I believe if price is turning where my stop loss is, then I must be close to understanding some of RTM materials Interesting thing about the W1 pinbar that I mentioned in post 120, the last move collected the stops above that and produced the decent bounce Onto the next opportunity. Please see chart.

Did I get the logic right here?

As always, thank you for all of your comments and continued guidance
